title: Cartesian exponent and restriction fibrations for Segal spaces
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, Kan complexes, homotopy fibers and weak homotopy equivalences from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the Kan model structure of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], and the Reedy model structure of [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure]. A simplicial space is a functor $V:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{sSet}$. It is a Segal space if it is Reedy fibrant and its consecutive-edge maps $V_n\to V_1\times_{V_0}\cdots\times_{V_0}V_1$ are weak homotopy equivalences for every $n\geq2$. For vertices $x,y$ of $V_0$, let $M_V(x,y)$ be the strict fiber of $(d_1,d_0):V_1\to V_0^2$. The homotopy category $hV$ has those vertices as objects, morphisms $\pi_0M_V(x,y)$, identity from $s_0$, and composition from the degree-two Segal map and $d_1$. Let $V_{\mathrm{eq}}\subseteq V_1$ be the union of components representing isomorphisms in $hV$.

For $n\geq0$ let $F(n)_k=\operatorname{Hom}_\Delta([k],[n])$, discrete in the inner direction, and let $cK$ denote the constant simplicial space on a simplicial set $K$. For simplicial spaces $A,V$, use the cartesian internal hom
$$(V^A)_{n,q}=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{sS}}(A\times F(n)\times c\Delta^q,V),$$
with operators given by precomposition. For every Segal space $V$ and every small simplicial space $A$, the internal hom $V^A$ is a Segal space. If $j:A\hookrightarrow B$ is degreewise injective in both simplicial directions, then restriction $V^B\to V^A$ is a Reedy fibration. In particular its degree-zero map $(V^B)_0\to(V^A)_0$ is a Kan fibration.

source.place: Sections 2.3-2.5 and Corollary 7.3 (Segal-space clause), proved using Theorem 7.1 and Section 10; printed pp. 6-7, 15-16, 22-24. Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this result.

proof.text: For a simplicial space $T$, write $\operatorname{Map}(T,X)_q=\operatorname{Hom}(T\times c\Delta^q,X)$, as in [lem-coef-simplicial-space-reedy-cartesian]. Evaluation at the identity of $[n]$ gives $\operatorname{Map}(F(n),X)=X_n$: its inverse sends a simplex $x\in X_{n,q}$ to the map whose value on $\alpha:[k]\to[n]$ is $X(\alpha)(x)$, in every inner degree by the simplicial operators of $x$. Naturality verifies these are inverse and commute with all operators. Define $G(n)$ to be the union of the consecutive copies of $F(1)$, glued at the common copies of $F(0)$. A map from this union is exactly a tuple of maps from the edges agreeing on their common endpoints. Thus $\operatorname{Map}(G(n),X)=X_1\times_{X_0}\cdots\times_{X_0}X_1$, and restriction from $F(n)$ is exactly the consecutive-edge map. For arbitrary simplicial spaces $A,T,X$, the displayed internal-hom formula gives a natural bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(T,X^A)=\operatorname{Hom}(A\times T,X)$: send $h:T\to X^A$ to the map whose value on $(a,t)\in A_{n,q}\times T_{n,q}$ is $h(t)(a,\mathrm{id}_{[n]},\mathrm{id}_{[q]})$. Conversely, given $k:A\times T\to X$, send $t\in T_{n,q}$ to the map taking $(a,\alpha,\beta)\in A_{r,s}\times\operatorname{Hom}_\Delta([r],[n])\times\operatorname{Hom}_\Delta([s],[q])$ to $k(a,T(\alpha,\beta)t)$. Naturality makes these inverse and makes the bijection commute with all maps of $A,T,X$. Evaluation in outer degree $n$ now identifies $\operatorname{Map}(F(n),X^T)$ with $\operatorname{Map}(T\times F(n),X)$; mapping out of the union gives $\operatorname{Map}(G(n),X^T)=\operatorname{Map}(T\times G(n),X)$. All these are isomorphisms of simplicial sets, with the stated restriction maps, not merely equivalences of components.

source.place: Sections 2.3 and 4.1, printed pp. 5-6 and 11; explicit evaluation, gluing, and the internal-hom adjunction on bidegree simplices.

proof.text: First prove Reedy fibrancy and the restriction-fibration assertion without using the Segal condition. Let $j:A\hookrightarrow B$ be any monomorphism and let $V$ be Reedy fibrant. To test whether $V^B\to V^A$ is a Reedy fibration, take any Reedy trivial cofibration $i:C\to D$ and a commutative lifting square against restriction. The internal-hom formula identifies that square with a map $(B\times C)\amalg_{A\times C}(A\times D)\to V$; a lift is precisely its extension to $B\times D$. The pushout product $j\mathbin{\square}i$ is a Reedy trivial cofibration by [lem-coef-simplicial-space-reedy-cartesian]. The map $V\to *$ lifts against it, by the weak-factorization-system characterization of Reedy fibrations in [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure]. This gives the required lift for every $i$. Taking $j:\varnothing\to T$ proves $V^T$ Reedy fibrant for every small $T$, because $V^{\varnothing}=*$ directly from the internal-hom formula.

source.place: Sections 2.4-2.5, printed pp. 6-7; pushout-product and lifting adjunction expanded.

proof.text: Put $f=\coprod_{n\geq2}(G(n)\hookrightarrow F(n))$, a monomorphism of small simplicial spaces, and take its localization model from [lem-coef-simplicial-space-localization-interval-criterion]. Its local objects are exactly the Segal spaces of the item. To check this carefully, for any Reedy fibrant $W$ the maps $r_n:\operatorname{Map}(F(n),W)\to\operatorname{Map}(G(n),W)$ are Kan fibrations by the mapping-space assertion of [lem-coef-simplicial-space-reedy-cartesian], since the spine inclusions are monomorphisms. The map $\operatorname{Map}(f,W)$ is their product. If $W$ is Segal, every $r_n$ is a trivial fibration by step 1, so their product lifts against every boundary inclusion by taking coordinatewise lifts; it is a trivial fibration by [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Conversely suppose $W$ is $f$-local. If $W_0$ is empty, the vertex maps force all $W_k$ to be empty, so both mapping spaces in each $r_n$ are empty and $r_n$ is the identity of the empty simplicial set. If $W_0$ has a vertex $x$, its totally degenerate simplices give compatible basepoints in both sides of every $r_n$. Fixing those basepoints in all coordinates except $n$ and projecting back exhibits $r_n$ as a retract, in the arrow category, of $\prod_m r_m$. That product is a weak equivalence by $f$-locality, and weak equivalences are retract closed by the model axioms in [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure]. Thus every $r_n$ is a weak equivalence, which is the Segal condition by step 1. This covers also empty and disconnected vertex spaces; no completeness condition has been imposed.

source.place: Section 10, opening paragraph, printed p. 23; Proposition 9.1 and Section 4.1. The coproduct-locality argument includes the empty-object case explicitly.

proof.text: For every $f$-local $W$, step 3 makes $W$ a Segal space. Step 2 makes $W^{F(1)}$ Reedy fibrant. For $n\geq2$, its consecutive-edge map identifies by step 1 with restriction $\operatorname{Map}(F(1)\times F(n),W)\to\operatorname{Map}(F(1)\times G(n),W)$. This is a weak equivalence by [lem-coef-segal-spine-interval-test]. Hence $W^{F(1)}$ is Segal, and therefore $f$-local by step 3. This verifies the additional hypothesis of [lem-coef-simplicial-space-localization-interval-criterion] for every local object, so the cartesian pushout product of two monomorphisms is a local equivalence whenever either factor is one.

source.place: Section 10 after Remark 10.2, Lemma 10.3, and Proposition 9.2, printed pp. 22-24; verification of the interval criterion.

proof.text: Let $A$ now be any small simplicial space and $V$ any Segal space. To prove that $V^A$ is $f$-local, test its terminal map against an arbitrary trivial cofibration $u:C\hookrightarrow D$ in the $f$-local model of [lem-coef-simplicial-space-localization-interval-criterion]. A map $C\to V^A$ is exactly a map $A\times C\to V$, and extending it to $D\to V^A$ is exactly extending that map to $A\times D\to V$. By step 4 the map $A\times u=(\varnothing\to A)\mathbin{\square}u$ is a monomorphism and an $f$-local equivalence. Since $V$ is local by step 3, $V\to *$ lifts against $A\times u$. The resulting extension proves the right lifting property against every local trivial cofibration. The model characterization in the cited node makes $V^A$ fibrant in the local model, hence $f$-local and Segal by step 3. This uses the given internal hom throughout, and applies also to $A=\varnothing$.

source.place: Corollary 7.3, printed p. 16, derived from Theorem 7.1 by the pushout-product adjunction; the lifting argument is written explicitly.

proof.text: For the monomorphism $j:A\hookrightarrow B$ in the item, step 2 already proves that restriction $V^B\to V^A$ is a Reedy fibration. In outer degree zero the matching diagram is empty, so the relative matching map is exactly $(V^B)_0\to(V^A)_0$. The fibration formula of [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure], in the Kan model structure [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], makes this a Kan fibration, as asserted.

source.place: Section 2.4, printed p. 6; degree-zero relative matching formula.

lean.statement: theorem cartesian_exponent (V : SimplicialSpace.{u}) (hV : IsSegal V) : (∀ A : SimplicialSpace.{u}, IsSegal ((ihom A).obj V)) ∧ ∀ (A B : SimplicialSpace.{u}) (j : A ⟶ B), (∀ n q : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ, Function.Injective ((j.app n).app q)) → IsReedyFibration ((MonoidalClosed.pre j).app V) ∧ Fibration (((MonoidalClosed.pre j).app V).app (op ⦋0⦌))
